newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says April trade deficit CZK 11.4 bln.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says April trade deficit CZK 11.4 bln.

text.p: The Czech trade deficit narrowed in April to 11.4 billion crowns from about 13.4 billion crowns in March on a strong year-on-year jump in exports, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Monday, quoting preliminary figures from the Czech customs administration.
He said exports for April showed a rise of 25.9 percent year-on-year, while imports rose 18.7 percent.
"I hope this is news to which the foreign exchange markets will react positively," Klaus told journalists after a meeting of economic ministers.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) reported last month that imports for the first quarter grew 8.0 percent, year-on-year, while exports were up only 0.6 percent.
The Czech crown has been under heavy downward pressure as the trade deficit has caused the already large current account deficit to grow to more than nine percent of gross domestic product.
The government in late April took a series of measures, including the imposition of deposits against selected imports of consumer goods, in an effort to curb the trade deficit.
